definitions.meaning: The number of individuals P at time t; the vertical axis of the logistic curve.
The largest population K the environment can support; the ceiling the curve levels at, written P = K.
The differential equation dP/dt = rP(1 - P/K) that governs logistic growth.
The rate of change dP/dt; it rises, peaks halfway to K, then falls to zero at P = K.
A population level where the growth rate is zero, so the population stops changing; P = K is the stable one here.
A grid of short ticks showing the growth direction at each population; steep low down, flat near K.
Steady removal of population every season; it drags the equilibrium down to a lower level.
The constant r in the logistic equation: the per-capita growth rate when the population is small.
One curve P(t) through the slope field for a given starting population; every solution curve settles at K.

mechanismSteps: The curve bends to the ceiling: the population grows almost exponentially at first, then bends over and levels exactly at P = K (s1).
The slope field funnels all starts: steep ticks low down and flat ticks near K guide low, middle and high starting curves to the same equilibrium (s2).
The equation brakes the growth: dP/dt = rP(1 - P/K) peaks halfway to K and falls to zero at P = K, which is what levels the curve (s3).
Harvesting drags the equilibrium down: steady removals lower the balancing level, and the population re-settles at the lower ceiling (s4).
objectives: Describe logistic growth: a population curve that bends over and levels at the carrying capacity K
Explain why the growth rate falls to zero at P = K, so K is the stable equilibrium every starting population is funnelled to
Use the slope field and the factor (1 - P/K) to predict where any starting population settles, including under harvesting
subject: math
title: Logistic growth: bending to the carrying capacity

trap.explanation: The slip: Early on the logistic curve looks just like exponential growth, so it is tempting to extrapolate the steepening rise for ever. The fix: As the population nears the carrying capacity K the growth rate falls to zero, so the curve bends over and levels at P = K, the stable equilibrium every starting population is funnelled to. In class, replay scene 1: freeze the curve where it bends and ask what the graph would look like if the early exponential rise continued - it would climb through the dashed ceiling and never level; the bending curve shows it cannot, so the growth rate must fall to zero at K first.
trap.misconception: The population keeps growing faster and faster like a pure exponential, so it never slows down or levels off.

workedExample: Work the bend from the equation. Step 1 (s1): at small P the factor (1 - P/K) is near 1, so the curve climbs almost exponentially. Step 2 (s3): halfway to K the growth rate peaks, then the factor shrinks and the rate falls. Step 3 (s1): at P = K the factor is zero, the rate is zero, and the curve levels at the carrying capacity.
